findings.why_it_matters: In the PDF, 'FORMAT 3' is an ordinary (non-bold, body-size) label paragraph that scopes the general rules that follow it inside 14.9.1.4 - exactly like 'FORMAT 1' / 'FORMAT 2' on pages 620 and 623, which the transcription renders as plain paragraphs. Promoting it to a level-2 markdown heading injects a phantom section into the document outline at the SAME level as '## 14.9.1.3 Syntax rules', so General rule 13) and everything after it appears to belong to a top-level section named 'FORMAT 3' rather than to 14.9.1.4, General rules. The transcription is overwhelmingly consistent the other way: 209 plain 'FORMAT n' label lines vs only 8 promoted to headings.

(The same fix applies to the other 7 promoted labels at lines 6280, 6284, 6288, 6298, 19800, 28029, 28033, which lie outside this batch.)

findings.why_it_matters: Four-component subclauses of a statement are transcribed at heading level 3 throughout 14.9 (### 14.9.3.1 .. ### 14.9.3.4 for ALLOCATE on page 616, ### 14.9.5.1 .. ### 14.9.5.4, ### 14.9.6.x, ### 14.9.8.x, and 14.9.2.1/14.9.2.2 on page 613 itself). Emitting 14.9.2.3 and 14.9.2.4 at level 2 makes them siblings of '## 14.9.2 ADD statement' instead of children of it, so the ADD statement's syntax rules and general rules detach from the ADD statement in any outline, TOC or anchor-walk built from the markdown.
